checks: For an h-three-cycle, missing xh(x) cannot be an edge of B because its image overlaps its tail; therefore the missing pair is good.
If all three head pairs are adjacent, the far-head restrictions force a reverse directed triangle, which gives a forbidden two-step path to the head.
A B-neighbor z of h(x) yields h(x)->h(z)->h^3(x)=x. The active packet boundary of x supplies a predecessor witnessing nonconvenience of h(x)->x, forcing the good direction x->h(x).
A six-vertex tree orbit has only factorizations two components of size three or three components of size two. The first has a forbidden h-two-cycle of tree centers.
For an h-six-cycle on three matching edges, orient even endpoints toward odd endpoints; no sink has its h-image with positive indegree.
For two h-three-cycles, any specified forced-good source can be the unique obstructive matching root; the other roots have h-images with indegree zero.
The forced good orientation is unique, hence compatible with one global canonical reference and unaffected by independently oriented other component orbits.
All completion-envelope predicates h and Far are defined in the original graph, so an added good first arc need not preserve the old far relation in the completed tournament.
Only tree-component orbits of at least eight vertices can contribute remaining zero gaps; the zero-set theorem requires at least three, giving twenty-four actual sources.

finite_orientation_check.scope: Abstract matching orientation certificates only, not SSNC graph construction or verification.
